newsitem.title: USA: Grist Mill sees flat FY 1997 revenues.
newsitem.headline: Grist Mill sees flat FY 1997 revenues.

text.p: Grist Mill Co chief executive Glen Bolander told shareholders to expect flat revenues in fiscal year 1997, but a shift in their source.
At the annual meeting on Tuesday, Bolander displayed a graphic showing revenues in fiscal 1997 would be $98 million, essentially the same as fiscal 1996 which ended May 31.

Revenue from the company's grocery business would, however, increase to $83 million in fiscal 1997 from $67 million the previous year, Bolander said, and revenue from the company's contract manufacturing business would decline to $15 million from $31 million in fiscal 1996.
"We anticipate our growth will principally come from our core products business and not from our contract manufacturing," Bolander said. He did not comment on the specifics of the graphic.
Bolander told Reuters before the meeting that he expected recent price cuts by major cereal makers to have only a limited effect on the company's revenues and earnings.
"We expect to see an average two to three percent decline in our pricing in our ready-to-eat cereal area," Bolander said.

"I expect a very nominal effect on our revenues and very little impact on our earnings because we're fairly well diversified over three product categories -- granola bars, fruit bars and cereals -- with each representing about one-third of our volume," he said.
